scenarioName: Geriatric Fall — Hip Fragility Fracture on Anticoagulation

scenarioStory.history: Home health aide arrived for a scheduled visit and found the patient on the kitchen floor. Patient reports tripping over a throw rug approximately 20 minutes prior; denies loss of consciousness, denies striking her head. Complains of severe right hip pain, unable to stand or bear weight.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find an 89-year-old female supine on the kitchen floor with obvious right leg deformity. She is alert, in visible pain, and denies head strike. → Primary survey and pain management completed: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, obtains a medication history revealing apixaban use, assesses neurovascular status of the injured leg, splints in position found, and administers weight-based fentanyl with cautious dosing given her age and anticoagulant therapy. → Splinted, medicated, transported with serial monitoring: Patient is packaged with a splinted right hip, pain well controlled, and transported with serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment given her anticoagulant use and elevated risk for occult hemorrhage.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Right hip pain after a ground-level fall, unable to bear weight

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find an 89-year-old female supine on the kitchen floor with obvious right leg deformity. She is alert, in visible pain, and denies head strike.

scenarioEvents.name: Primary survey and pain management completed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, obtains a medication history revealing apixaban use, assesses neurovascular status of the injured leg, splints in position found, and administers weight-based fentanyl with cautious dosing given her age and anticoagulant therapy.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey; rule out life threats before focusing on the hip
Obtain medication history; identify apixaban (anticoagulant) use
Assess pallor, pulse, capillary refill, sensation, and movement of right leg before splinting
Splint right hip/leg in position found before any further movement
Fentanyl 55 mcg IV (55 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
Titrate opioid cautiously; monitor for hypoventilation given her comorbidities

scenarioEvents.name: Splinted, medicated, transported with serial monitoring
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is packaged with a splinted right hip, pain well controlled, and transported with serial vital sign and neurologic reassessment given her anticoagulant use and elevated risk for occult hemorrhage.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and neuro status serially en route; monitor for occult hemorrhage
Transport to appropriate trauma-capable facility per field triage guideline

scenarioEvents.name: Anticoagulant use not identified, serial monitoring omitted
scenarioEvents.description: The crew splints and medicates the hip but never asks about medications, missing the apixaban history. Without recognizing the bleeding risk, serial reassessment is skipped en route, and the patient develops evolving hemorrhagic shock without early warning signs.
relatedChecklist: Recognize occult hemorrhagic shock; establish IV access and initiate fluid bolus
